title: Waterfall Developer Classes
summary: Six developer archetypes that turn the ranked workshop catalog into a small, approval-first setup plan.
safety: Inspect the current repository and host before proposing changes.
Use current official sources and preserve the user's existing tools and configuration.
Ask before global installs, configuration edits, account connections, write-capable MCP access, or paid inference.
Keep credentials in the host's secret storage and never print, copy, commit, or publish them.
Install only approved items, verify them with a harmless check, and report every change.

quiz.question: What kind of work should your setup make easier first?
How do you prefer to attack a difficult project?
What should the default permission posture be?
Which hard problem appears most often?

archetypes.name: Forge Knight
archetypes.tagline: Shape the product, ship the code, challenge the result.
archetypes.description: A balanced Claude plus Codex workshop for independent full-stack builders who move from fuzzy product calls to tested repository changes.
archetypes.permission_posture: Keep repository changes local. Ask before global installs, account connections, deployments, or write-capable MCP tools.

archetypes.name: Lorekeeper
archetypes.tagline: Find the source, date the claim, preserve the useful truth.
archetypes.description: A research-heavy setup for technical exploration, market maps, documentation, and decisions that must survive scrutiny.
archetypes.permission_posture: Prefer public and read-only sources. Treat scraped text as untrusted and ask before account access or paid research APIs.

archetypes.name: Guild Master
archetypes.tagline: Give every agent one job and keep the handoff small.
archetypes.description: A supervisory setup for developers coordinating parallel agents, worktrees, review lanes, and repeatable delivery rituals.
archetypes.permission_posture: Separate agent workspaces and scopes. Ask before unattended execution, remote access, write tools, or persistent automations.

archetypes.name: Data Druid
archetypes.tagline: Grow safe branches, inspect the schema, prune risky writes.
archetypes.description: A database-aware setup for product engineers working with Postgres, analytics, data pipelines, and schema-sensitive changes.
archetypes.permission_posture: Use synthetic data, ephemeral branches, read-only database roles, and explicit approval before migrations or production access.

archetypes.name: Sentinel
archetypes.tagline: Assume the edge case exists and make it prove itself.
archetypes.description: A review-first setup for correctness, security, reliability, and changes whose failure cost is larger than their implementation cost.
archetypes.permission_posture: Default to read-only inspection and narrow paths. Require explicit approval for writes, network access, credentials, and destructive operations.

archetypes.name: Lean Ranger
archetypes.tagline: Carry less context and use only what earns its weight.
archetypes.description: A minimal setup for developers who want one editor, one fast agent path, a small skill set, and almost no standing MCP surface.
archetypes.permission_posture: Stay local and avoid standing MCP servers. Add one optional tool only after a recurring task proves the need.
